subject: Private deploy release orchestration + test harness alignment
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@acme-systems.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@cloud-integrators.io>
Date: 2027-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy release orchestration + test harness alignment

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. As discussed in our call last week, Acme needs a tightly scripted release path for the VPC/on-prem package — we must be able to validate a production-ready rollout inside our air-gapped datacenter and certify network ACLs, MTLS between services, and key rotation steps.

Can your team review the proposed module split and the test harness we sketched? I attached a quick export of the checklist we keep for SOC-style reviews. High-level asks:
- A deterministic Terraform plan for core networking + subnets (no runtime host provisioning)
- Helm charts that support immutable release metadata and can be validated offline
- An Ansible-driven smoke-test harness we can run in a lab to validate connectivity and KV cache warmup before cutting traffic

Target: we need a validated handoff to Acme engineering by 2027-08-20 so their compliance window stays on track.

Attachment: privstack-acme-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Rajesh
CTO, Acme Systems
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy release orchestration + test harness alignment

Rajesh — appreciate the clarity. We'll take ownership of a review and produce a short rollout playbook aligned to your checklist. Planning notes and immediate next steps:

1) We will split the review into: Terraform networking contract, Helm release semantics, and the Ansible test harness. Each area will get a short conformance checklist.
2) Dev will produce a minimized terraform plan (terraform plan -out=network.plan) we can share.
3) Grace will drive security checks and provide the MTLS/cert rotation requirements.
4) Mina will scope the smoke-test scenarios and provide an Ansible artifact we can execute in your lab.

Can you confirm we have permission to share the minimal IaC artifacts with your integration partner (Aditi Shah) for in-lab validation? Once confirmed, we'll open a GitHub PR and a release candidate build.

Regards,
Irene
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@acme-systems.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy release orchestration + test harness alignment

Irene / Rajesh,

Quick technical reply with what I'll deliver by EOD tomorrow:
- Terraform: a small, opinionated module set (priv-vpc/core, priv-vpc/bastion, priv-vpc/egress) with explicit outputs for route tables and service endpoints. I'll include a change log PDF (tf-modules-change-log.pdf). The modules avoid any implicit instance creation — we only emit networking, subnets, and firewall resources.

- Helm: updated chart values and a release notes template that ensures image digests and release-ids are embedded in Chart metadata. See attachment: privstack-helm-values.yaml (yaml). This enables offline verification in your lab since the chart contains immutable references.

- Ansible: a scoped test harness (ansible playbooks + inventory) that will run the smoke tests you listed: MTLS handshake, KV cache warmup validation, prefix-caching and long-tail latency check. I will supply an artifact (ansible-playbook-test-harness.zip) and a short runbook.

Notes on CI gating: we propose a two-stage gate for private deployments — (1) automated static validation + unit tests (GH actions) that produce an artifact, (2) a release-bundle build that is hand-verified by our release engineer and uploaded to a secure artifact bucket your integrator can pull from. If Acme needs, we can sign the artifacts with our KMS before delivery.

PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/privstack/pull/642 (contains the terraform modules and helm changes).

- Dev

Subject: Re: Private deploy release orchestration + test harness alignment

Adding security acceptance criteria and a suggested test matrix. High level: we need deterministic artifact signing + an artifact-to-release mapping that the customer can independently verify. Specifics below:

- Identity: all service principals must be created via a documented step with key material rotated at install time. For air-gapped installs, provide an offline key-import step.
- MTLS: provide a validation play that attempts mutual TLS on a sample 5-minute window and writes a signed attestation to the local audit folder.
- Network: ensure default-deny on non-essential control plane ports; include a small iptables/ebpf checklist for host-level hardening.
- Regression: include a post-install latency smoke test that captures 95/99 percentiles for 1K synthetic requests.

I'll attach a short checklist to the PR and add a Confluence checklist entry: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PRIV/Security+Acceptance+Checks

Grace
Sr Manager, Security & Compliance

Thanks team — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Aditi confirms she can run the Ansible harness in our lab next Tuesday (2027-08-17). Please proceed with the PR and mark it as release-candidate/ACME-2027-08 in the branch name so our compliance team can reference it.

Action items I will own: lab scheduling, compliance evidence ingestion.
Action items for Redwood: open the PR, attach the change log and helm values, produce the signed artifact if possible, and add the Confluence checklist entry for the MTLS attestation step.

We are comfortable with the proposed two-stage CI gate. If you can get the artifacts to us by 2027-08-15, we'll aim for a verification window and handoff by 2027-08-20.

Regards,
Rajesh
CTO, Acme Systems
